findings.question: Which build / call path supplies the tag-3 arm of driver_ctor 0x5ce01f0, left open as edge 1 of the time-context writers packet (#2948)?
findings.answer: SETTLED, with the premise corrected.  The tag-3 arm is not a wrapper of an already-built context: the tail at 0x5ce06a0 writes only [out] = 3 and [out+8] = r15 and touches no driver field -- it is the constructor's failure encoding.  Its whole supply is two OS-failure routes inside the poll variant, both carrying (errno << 32) | 2 in [out+8], reached from runtime builds that all drive the poll variant with time enabled.  The builder converts a ctor tag-3 into its own error {[+0] = 2, [+8] = error word}, and the wrappers divert on that tag, so a tag-3 outcome surfaces as a runtime-build failure: no caller ever receives a tag-3 context.
findings.variant_gate: Only the poll variant reaches the tail.  cmpb $0, cfg+8 at 0x5ce0207 / je 0x5ce0332 at 0x5ce020b sends the variant-0 arm straight to the shared install sequence; the all-encoding branch census into 0x5ce06a0, boundary-verified against the ctor's own disassembly, is exactly jo 0x5ce022c and je 0x5ce0670 plus the fall-through from the close call at 0x5ce069a -- all in the poll path.  The raw candidate at 0x5ce069e is a byte inside that call's displacement and fails boundary verification.
findings.route_r1_poll_new_failure: Poll::new 0x5ceeae0 fails (epoll_create1 / eventfd / epoll_ctl): the ctor loads its word0, neg at 0x5ce0229 overflows exactly on INT64_MIN and jo 0x5ce022c jumps to the tail with r15 = word1.  All three Poll::new error exits write {INT64_MIN, (errno << 32) | 2} (encoder pins at 0x5ceeb9d..0x5ceebb3, shared encoder 0x5ceebd4..0x5ceebea, 0x5ceec0f..0x5ceec25) and close their own partial fds, so [out+8] = (errno << 32) | 2.
findings.route_r2_attach_failure: The signal-attach body 0x5ce71f0 lazily initialises a global signal state (flag dword 0x64fee38, fd dword 0x64fee24, object 0x64fee20, via lazy_init 0x5cdf582), dups the global fd with fcntl(F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC = 0x406, min 3) through GOT slot 0x64e8a18 and registers the dup on the poll's epoll through slot 0x64e12c0 (event flags 0x80002001, data 1), then wraps the registration in a fresh 0x10-byte Arc and copies the poll pair plus {+0x20 = Arc, +0x28 = dup fd} into its result.  Its two failure exits write {INT64_MIN, (errno << 32) | 2} (0x5ce72a4..0x5ce72ba for the fcntl failure, 0x5ce72f8..0x5ce730e for the epoll_ctl failure).  The ctor's cmp at 0x5ce02c2..0x5ce02d6 catches word0 == INT64_MIN, falls through to the cleanup (dup fd close at 0x5ce02df, registry Vec element drop loop, buffer free and eventfd close at 0x5ce067b..0x5ce069a) and falls through to the tail with r15 = the same error word.
findings.route_r3_value_unreachable: The je at 0x5ce0670 sits in the post-registration block entered only from the jne at 0x5ce02d9 (attach success).  The block stashes rdx / r15 at [rsp+0xc8] / [rsp+0xd0] (0x5ce05ca / 0x5ce05d2), increments the registration Arc's +8 word with a lock cmpxchg spin (0x5ce05e6..0x5ce0609), reloads rax = [rsp+0xc8] and r15 = [rsp+0xd0], then inc rcx (0x5ce066a) / cmp rax, rcx (0x5ce066d).  rcx on this path is the movabs INT64_MIN of 0x5ce02c2: the register-write scan finds no rcx write inside the block before the inc, and the only other rcx writes in the ctor span are inside the install sequence, which this path enters only after the compare (jmp 0x5ce0676 -> 0x5ce0382).  rax is the attach word0 -- on success the Poll::new capacity (0x400 under the artifact's own config), the failure word having been diverted at 0x5ce02d9; and the rdx-write scan finds no rdx write between the load at 0x5ce02cc and the stash, so the stashed word is the attach word0 itself.  capacity == INT64_MIN + 1 can never hold, so the je never fires; it is a compiler-emitted counted compare whose exit the real flow leaves through 0x5ce0676.
findings.supply_chain: driver_ctor's only callers are the builder's two call sites (0x5cf9669, 0x5cf96eb).  The builder has no direct callers; its only pointer reference is the .rela.dyn type-8 addend at GOT slot 0x64e1760, and its start's only imm64 occurrence in the whole file is that addend field.  The slot is called at exactly three sites: 0x15d7026 and 0x15d70c2 in the wrapper body under FDE 0x15d6fd0..0x15d8447, and 0x2ae16f2 under FDE 0x2ae1690..0x2ae27b2.
findings.config_supply: cfg_ctor 0x5cf93f0's only callers are the same three wrapper sites.  It writes the flavour argument to [bcfg+0xe4] (0x5cf948e), INT64_MIN to [bcfg+0x20], capacity 0x400 to [bcfg+0x60] (0x5cf94a3), 0 to [bcfg+0] (0x5cf94ab) and 0 to the dword at [bcfg+0xe5] (0x5cf9521).  Each wrapper then stores the u16 constant 0x0101 at bcfg+0xe5 (0x15d700c, 0x15d70a8, 0x2ae16d6): variant byte 1, tag byte 1.  The builder assembles the ctor config from [bcfg+0x60] (word0) and the u16 at [bcfg+0xe5] (cfg+8), with cfg+0xa = 1 at site 1 (0x5cf964e) and 0 at site 2 (0x5cf96c5) and cfg+0xb = [bcfg+0xe7]; path (b) to site 2 first calls builder_precall 0x5cf5db0 (0x5cf9697), selected because [bcfg+0] = 0 != 1 (cmp at 0x5cf9627).  The ctor's reads through its config pointer are exactly cfg+8 (variant, 0x5ce0207), cfg word0 (0x5ce0211) and cfg+9 (tag, 0x5ce03f6).
findings.conversion: At builder site 1 a ctor tag of 3 (cmp 0x5cf967e) loads eax = 2 and ecx = 8 (0x5cf9688 / 0x5cf968d) and jumps to the shared stores {[out+8] = r15, [out] = 2} at 0x5cfa1c5 / 0x5cfa1c9; at site 2 the stores are inline (0x5cf970a / 0x5cf970e).  Both wrappers compare the builder result's tag against 2 and jump to their own error paths (0x15d7039 / 0x15d7041, 0x15d70c8 / 0x15d70d0, 0x2ae16f8 / 0x2ae1700).  A tag-3 outcome surfaces as a runtime-build failure; no caller receives a tag-3 context, nothing is installed from one, and re-initialisation of a wrapped context cannot arise.

open_edges: The two wrapper bodies' source-level identity (which node subsystem's runtime build each is) is not pinned: no Location static for either was recovered in this packet.  The claim is limited to the call graph, their three builder call sites and the config bytes they write.

cfg+0xa (1 at builder site 1, 0 at site 2) and cfg+0xb (= [bcfg+0xe7], 0 under the artifact's own config constructor) are assembled into the ctor config but never read by the ctor; their consumer, if any, is outside this question.

The builder's [bcfg+0] == 1 arm (r13 = [bcfg+8], no builder_precall) is not supplied by the artifact's own config constructor, which writes 0 at [bcfg+0]; whether a config built outside the artifact could select it is outside the artifact and not claimed.
The producer of the global signal state (what creates the fd published at 0x64fee24 before lazy_init 0x5cdf582 runs) is not traced; this packet pins only the attach body's use of it.

Why the compiler emits a counted compare against INT64_MIN + 1 in the post-registration block is stated at byte level only; the value-unreachability of route R3 does not depend on the source-level shape.
